comment: No catch-all rewrite. Every route the site has is now a real prerendered file, written
from the same content metadata the router reads, so the rewrite's only remaining job was
answering unknown addresses with the landing page at HTTP 200 — a soft 404, which a search
engine indexes as a duplicate of the front door. Without it Firebase serves dist/404.html
trailingSlash is false so /docs/reference/flow is served as itself. Firebase's default is
to 301 it to /docs/reference/flow/, and the address bar then disagrees with both the
canonical link in the page and the route the file was rendered for — which cost every
reader a redirect and threw away the prerendered markup instead of hydrating it.
